# Phase 2 results (generated by scripts/20_phase2.py)

## 2a. Pull-forward / pantry loading

- Post-window rule: weeks t1+1..t1+4 after the run ends, truncated at the first promoted or unobserved week. 51% of events (25,347) have a full clean 4-week window; 14% have none (another promotion started the very next week).
- Headline (events with a full clean post window, n=25,347):
  - In-week (run) lift: **117.5%** (95% CI 114.2% to 120.8%)
  - Net lift over run + 4 weeks: **120.5%** (95% CI 117.1% to 123.8%)
  - Pull-forward ratio = 1 - net/in-week: **-2.5%** (95% CI -2.9% to -2.1%)
  - Mean incremental units per event: in-week 58.2, post-window +1.5, net 59.7
- Reading: the naive in-week figure UNDERSTATES true incrementality by 2.5%. A positive ratio means post-promotion weeks dip below baseline (stock-up); a negative one means they stay above it (carry-over).
- Local-demand check: in the 4 weeks BEFORE a promotion the baseline residual averages +0.35 units/week (promotions land in locally strong weeks); in the 4 weeks after it averages +0.34 units/week. Subtracting the pre-residual from the post-window gives an adjusted pull-forward ratio of **+0.1%** (95% CI -0.4% to +0.5%). Still no dip.

## 2c. Where does the lift come from: new buyers or bigger baskets?

- Identity: ln(units/baseline) = ln(hhs/baseline_hhs) + ln(units-per-hh / baseline). Both baselines are the Phase 1 gradient-boosting models (units and households fitted with the same design on the same clean weeks).
- Events with meaningful lift (log lift > 0.10): 37,932 of 49,384. Among them, the households component explains on average **91%** of the log lift (median 93%).
- Classification: **95% penetration-driven**, 5% volume-driven.

### Do volume-driven promotions show more pull-forward than penetration-driven ones?

| driver      |   n_events |   in_week_incr_mean |   post_incr_mean |   pullforward_ratio |     lo |     hi |
|:------------|-----------:|--------------------:|-----------------:|--------------------:|-------:|-------:|
| volume      |        971 |              16.773 |           -0.265 |               0.016 | -0.075 |  0.103 |
| penetration |      19899 |              74.197 |            2.942 |              -0.040 | -0.044 | -0.036 |

- Difference (volume minus penetration) in pull-forward ratio: **+5.5%** (95% bootstrap CI -3.7% to +14.3%, bootstrap p = 0.228).
- Welch t-test on per-event post/in-week ratio (clipped to +/-3): volume mean -0.054 vs penetration +0.071, t = -2.52, p = 0.0119.

## 2d. Limitations surfaced by the data

- 22% of events have usable control stores; Method B is a cross-check, not the headline.
- 51% of events have a clean 4-week post window; pull-forward is measured on those, and they are events followed by a promotion gap, which may differ from back-to-back promotions.
- Promotions are not randomly assigned; promo frequency correlates +0.29 with seasonal demand (Phase 0), handled by week-of-year features but not provably removed.
- Cannibalisation across the 55 UPCs in a category is NOT measured here (out of scope; would need a category-level model).
